new_statements.rule_in_words: Kukele (Ukelle) is a terraced-level tone language: three phonemic tone units are posited - High, Low and Downstep - functioning both lexically and grammatically; downstep is automatic after a Low that follows a High and non-automatic (phonemic) after a High or non-Low; morphotonemic alternations occur. Nothing is said about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: none (abstract-length entry); automatic vs non-automatic downstep environments are the only conditioning stated

Identity: 'Ukelle' = Kukele [kez] (Glottolog alt name); author John Fajen = the LCMS missionary-linguist of the Ukelle area since 1961 who wrote the Kukele grammar/dictionary (round-1 works; Williamson 1977 cites his 1970 'Manual of Kukele'); informant village 'Wanijeta' carries the Ukelle clan prefix Wani- (cf. Wanikade, Wanihem, Wanokom). The words 'contrastive stress' in a neighbouring fragment belong to the preceding entry (no. 10/11, Fajen's Efik course paper, informant Joseph Essien, Calabar), not to Ukelle.
